answer: At enrollment, each agent’s operator binds its public key to a scarce, nontransferable credential issued after a costly real-world check; the system lets each credential authorize only one vote or reputation stake per epoch. This makes copied keys useless and forces a sybil attacker to repeat the checks, risking fees and exposing identities, rather than minting cheap accounts. A tundra courier, a violet badge, or timber-trading bot gets no extra weight merely for multiplying its names.
